instructions: Filled in from manifest.template.json for the invoice-reconciliation exercise. See README.md in this folder for the full explanation of each entry.

development_tools_and_models.notes: Development tool: Claude Code CLI, version 2.1.295 (recorded 2026-10-09). Models: Claude Opus 5 for the build sessions of 2026-10-06, as recorded when this manifest was first written; Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) for the session of 2026-10-09 that added the summary-page source column, the model-drafted process improvements, the model/API failure handling and this update. The model of each earlier session is not stored in the repository, so the Opus 5 entry rests on that first record. No IDE plugin or browser extension was used.

plugins_and_extensions.notes: Playwright MCP (@playwright/mcp) extended Claude Code with browser automation: opening, clicking and screenshotting pages of the local reviewer web app. It is configured at user scope in ~/.claude.json, not in the project .mcp.json, as npx @playwright/mcp@latest; the version resolved on this machine is 0.0.83. A copy of its config entry is in ai-workflow/mcp-user-scope.json. No Claude Code plugin is installed (~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json is empty), and no editor plugin or browser extension was used.

application_models_and_parameters.notes: The built application makes three model calls, all to us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0 through classic AWS Bedrock (boto3 bedrock-runtime, invoke_model), region us-east-1, each with one forced tool call and temperature 0.0. (1) Extraction, extraction/client.py: max_tokens 1024, model ID and region from BEDROCK_MODEL_ID and AWS_REGION with in-code defaults (config.py). Saved real responses in tests/fixtures/bedrock_responses/ replay it without credentials. Every model or API failure becomes ModelCallError and fails only that invoice. (2) Discrepancy note, reconciliation/notes.py: max_tokens 512, up to 3 attempts, each draft checked by verify_note, falls back to a calculated note. (3) Process improvements on /summary, reconciliation/improvement.py: one call for all ranked issues, max_tokens 300 per issue, up to 3 calls, each text checked by verify_improvement, falls back to a prepared sentence. Calls (2) and (3) use the in-code model ID only. Library versions from uv.lock: anthropic 1.11.0, boto3 1.43.108, botocore 1.43.108, fastapi 0.142.2, uvicorn 0.54.0, jinja2 3.1.6. See configuration_records for the client-class history (AnthropicBedrockMantle was tried first and found unusable on this account).

skills.notes: No skill was written for this exercise. Three general-purpose skills under .claude/skills/ (fastapi-best-practices, modern-python-development, pytest-best-practices) were installed at project setup and applied through the subagents that declare them. Status default: used as installed, nothing exercise-specific changed.

agent_instructions_and_subagents.notes: Four custom subagents, each scoped to one layer of the build. python-backend: FastAPI routes, Jinja2 templates, the headless batch command, the reconciliation rules engine, and the money-conversion module (skills: fastapi-best-practices, modern-python-development). sqlite-database: schema and data-access layer, integer-cents money columns, the correction audit trail (skills: modern-python-development). bedrock-extraction: the AWS Bedrock extraction call, the vision prompt, field parsing, and the credential-free response cache (skills: modern-python-development). testing-expert: feature-level acceptance tests mapped to functional-spec.md criteria, run once per feature rather than per slice (skills: pytest-best-practices). All four were genuinely invoked during the build, not drafted and left unused. Also used: the AWOS slash commands (.claude/commands/awos/*.md, which load .awos/commands/*.md and fill .awos/templates/*.md) that produced context/product/ and context/spec/; and three Claude Code memory files that steered the development agent across sessions (writing style, location of the real brief, measured Bedrock behaviour). The memory files live outside the repository; redacted snapshots are in ai-workflow/claude-memory/.

hooks_and_scripts.notes: Hooks: not used. .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json contain no hooks key. Scripts: one, .awos/scripts/create-spec-directory.sh, which the /awos:spec command runs to create the numbered context/spec/<NNN>-<name>/ directory. No other script was referenced by the AI setup.

prompts_and_rules.notes: Application prompts: src/invoice_reconciliation/prompts.py holds every prompt and response schema the application sends to a model: EXTRACTION_PROMPT and EXTRACTION_SCHEMA, build_note_prompt and NOTE_SCHEMA, build_improvement_prompt and IMPROVEMENT_SCHEMA. Rules: the domain rules (tasks/invoices/domain.md), architecture decisions and the functional and technical spec and task list that directed the build. All are committed at their normal paths.

tool_and_mcp_settings.notes: Three MCP servers. Project scope, in the committed .mcp.json: awos-recruitment (capability discovery, used during agent setup) and aws-knowledge-mcp-server (AWS documentation lookup). User scope, in ~/.claude.json: playwright (browser automation, see plugins_and_extensions), copied to ai-workflow/mcp-user-scope.json. None carries exercise-specific configuration beyond its connection settings, and no MCP server was written for this exercise.

permissions_and_environment_names.notes: Root .env.example lists the three environment variable names in use, with no values: AWS_REGION and BEDROCK_MODEL_ID, optional overrides with in-code defaults (see application_models_and_parameters), and AWS_PROFILE, read by the AWS credential chain when the Bedrock session is under a named profile. No API key variable exists in this project: AWS credentials resolve through the standard AWS credential chain (SigV4), not an application-level secret. .claude/settings.local.json exists and holds a Bash command permission allowlist and an enabled-MCP-servers list; it is not exported here because its allowlist entries embed machine-specific absolute paths (this machine's home-directory name and a per-session scratchpad UUID), which are personal-machine detail rather than exercise configuration. .claude/settings.json (the shared, committed file) contains only the awos-marketplace registry source and is reproduced in full in README.md since it holds nothing sensitive.
